notes: Libretto by Lorenzo Da Ponte (1787). Words follow the Schirmer vocal score's spelling and punctuation, and its repeats of words and lines. Where the print differs from the libretto the words follow the print: Leporello "bei giovinetti" (libretto giovanotti), "Cioccolate!" (libretto Cioccolata!) and "Gianotta" (libretto Giannotta); Zerlina "quest' affar" (printed as two words) and her added "sì,"; Masetto "Tocca, tocca!" (not in the libretto); Leporello's "Viva la liberta," in bar 120-121, printed without the accent (sung libertà). The piece ends on the last bar before the Minuetto: Don Giovanni's "ballerini" is cut there, its first syllables "balle-" sung in this piece and "-rini!" on the first bar of the next ("Meco tu dei ballare"). IPA, word meanings and translations were drafted for this app (S30) and the IPA was checked against Castel. IPA follows sung Italian conventions: stressed syllable marked, elisions (two words on one note in the score) joined with ‿, open e/o as ɛ/ɔ. Translation literal, for meaning.
